papers.title: Romantic Partner's Body Odor and Relationship Quality.
papers.abstract: As a powerful medium for nonverbal social communication, body odors convey important cues about our romantic partner's emotions. Since understanding each other's emotions is crucial for romantic relationships, body odors may foster attachment and connection in these contexts. Using a survey study with 206 participants, we explored how the odor of a romantic partner influenced relationship quality. Specifically, we investigated whether individuals' beliefs about their partner's body odor were associated with explicit relationship quality indicators (relationship satisfaction, emotional and sexual intimacy) controlling for partner's other traits. Our results showed the importance of thinking of a romantic partner's odor as pleasant for sexual intimacy above and beyond other traits. We also provide preliminary evidence that the mere evaluation of a partner's body odor was associated with feelings of safety and sexual arousal, which in turn predicted greater emotional and sexual intimacy, respectively. The present study advances our understanding of how body odors contribute to romantic chemistry and opens the way for more nuanced investigations.

papers.title: The Burden of Chronic Cough in Patients With Interstitial Lung Disease: a US Survey-Based Analysis of Its Effects on Daily Life and Emotional and Social Well-Being.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Chronic cough (≥8 weeks) is highly prevalent among patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) and non-IPF interstitial lung disease (ILD) and imposes significant physical, social, and psychological burden. Research characterizing the burden of chronic cough in patients with IPF and non-IPF ILD from the patient perspective is limited. RESEARCH QUESTION: What is the multidimensional burden of chronic cough in patients living with IPF or non-IPF ILD? STUDY DESIGN AND METHODS: An online cross-sectional survey was distributed to adults from June to July 2025 via the Pulmonary Fibrosis Foundation's US Community Registry. Eligibility required a self-reported diagnosis of IPF or non-IPF ILD and chronic cough. Multiple-choice and open-text questions spanned six domains: demographics, disease history, cough characteristics, daily life impact, social/emotional and long-term impact, and healthcare experience. RESULTS: A total of 197 participants completed the survey: 75.63% reported a diagnosis of IPF, 21.32% reported non-IPF ILD, and 3.05% were awaiting further ILD diagnosis. Participants reported cough-related interference with daily activities (76.15%) and sleep disruption (79.69%) within the preceding week. Emotional burden was frequently reported: 95.94% of participants had cough-induced worry, 75.13% had depression, sadness, or low mood, and 67.01% reported avoiding social situations because of cough. Additionally, 60.91% of participants reported that chronic cough affected their platonic relationships, and 55.33% reported impact on their ability or desire to maintain physical or intimate relationships. To treat cough, participants reported using an average of 2.7 therapeutic classes historically and 2.0 classes currently, with many reporting limited or no relief. papers.title: "Turn that down a few notches": A qualitative analysis of uncertainty and psychosocial burden among non-BRCA previvors.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Risk reducing decisions impact previvors' identity, family experiences, and relationships. These decisions are especially challenging for non-BRCA previvors, who face vague guidelines and limited evidence. This qualitative study explored non-BRCA previvors' attitudes toward family planning, relationships, and the burden of previvor status. METHODS: Previvors with non-BRCA mutations (Lynch-related, PALB2, RAD51C, BRIP1, CHEK2) were recruited from an urban gynecologic oncology clinic. We conducted semi-structured telephone interviews which were transcribed verbatim. Two investigators independently coded a subset of interviews, resolved discrepancies with a moderator blinded to study background, and then refined the codebook and applied across all transcripts to identify themes. RESULTS: Twenty-one previvors completed interviews (median age 39). Three overarching themes emerged: impact of previvor status on mental health, on personal identity, and impact of medical experience on decision making. Those considering future fertility worried about assisted reproductive technology (ART) cost and time pressure from risk reduction timelines; those not pursuing fertility worried about early menopause and mutation transmission to children. Previvor status impacted romantic relationships differently, with some describing strains caused by altered family planning and cancer prevention timelines, while others feeling no impact. Previvors emphasized the physician-patient relationship and shared decision-making. Many expressed frustrations regarding access to reliable data amid unclear guidelines. The lower penetrance of the non-BRCA did not lessen the psychosocial burden of previvor status in our cohort. CONCLUSIONS: Family planning, relationships, and previvor burden are central concerns for previvors. papers.title: High-precision 81Kr dating overcomes radiocarbon limits in Late Pleistocene groundwater.
papers.abstract: Groundwater preserves continental hydroclimate signals, but its use as a Late Pleistocene archive is limited by uncertainties in radiocarbon (14C) dating caused by carbon geochemical processes. The noble gas isotope 81Kr has simpler transport behavior, yet its effective dating limit was traditionally ∼50 thousand years (ka) because of analytical constraints. Here, we extended the 81Kr dating lower limit to ∼10 ka using high-precision atom trap trace analysis, thus covering the entire Late Pleistocene. We conducted a direct 14C-81Kr comparison in the North China Plain. Within the 10- to 30-ka range, 81Kr independently validates 14C ages; beyond this range, it provides reliable ages for older groundwater. The dual-tracer approach reduces model uncertainty in 14C correction and identifies mixing-affected samples. After screening, groundwater δ18O records closely match polar ice-core climate archives. High-precision 81Kr dating, combined with 14C, offers a robust age framework for reconstructing Late Pleistocene hydroclimate.

papers.title: Knowledge, attitude, and behaviours concerning mpox from an online survey among MSM in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR).
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Human monkeypox (mpox), a viral zoonotic infectious disease, was declared a public health emergency of international concern. Men who have sex with men (MSM) were most affected by mpox during the global outbreak. This study aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and behaviours concerning mpox among the MSM population in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (EMR). METHODS: This was a cross-sectional study of MSM residing in countries of the EMR. Participants were recruited through non-governmental organisations, dating applications, and LGBTQ+ websites between July and October 2023. Data on behaviours, perceptions, access to healthcare, socio-demographics, and medical characteristics related to mpox were collected online via LimeSurvey. The outcome was high mpox knowledge whereby a score greater than 12 of 17 was considered as high mpox knowledge score. Adaptive Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator logistic regression was used to predict participants' knowledge about mpox. Model discrimination and calibration were assessed. RESULTS: A total of 643 MSM participants of median age 31 (IQR:26-37) were included in the study. Among study participants, 131 (20.4%) had high mpox knowledge. Key predictors of high mpox knowledge score were being 31-40 years old, employed, in a relationship, thinking mpox vaccine is safe, and knowing someone infected with mpox. The model had good discrimination AUC = 0.812 (95%CI:0.77-0.85) and calibration C-slope = 1.073 (95%CI:0.87-1.27). CONCLUSION: This study identified gaps and predictors of high mpox knowledge score among MSM in the EMR. These findings provide new insights needed to raise awareness and inform targeted public health interventions to reduce the spread of mpox.

papers.title: Multiple spermatophore transfer during prolonged mating in the apterous neotropical cricket Unacla meridionalis (Desutter-Grandcolas 1994) (Orthoptera: Grylloidea: Phalangopsidae).
papers.abstract: Phalangopsidae comprises over 1,136 species of crickets, but reproductive behavior has been documented for only a few species. Here, we describe the mating behavior of Unacla meridionalis (Desutter-Grandcolas 1994), an apterous, nocturnal cricket endemic to the Brazilian Atlantic Forest. We analyzed 15 mating trials conducted under controlled laboratory conditions, including courtship, copulation, and post-copulation behaviors. During courtship, a male performs dorsoventral vibrations of the body and touching with the antennae, while a female palpates the abdominal tergites of the male; spermatophores are transferred during subsequent copulations; after the mating pair separated, females consumed the spermatophores in 87% of the encounters, which contrasts with the typical spermatophore consumption by males in other phalangopsid species and suggests that the spermatophore may represent a post-nuptial gift. The total mating event lasted approximately 2 h, representing a considerably long duration. These findings expand our understanding of the diversity of reproductive strategies within Phalangopsidae and underscore the evolutionary significance of extended mating and paternal investment in apterous crickets.

papers.title: "The Third Person in the Room": Supportive Fathers' Experiences of Breastfeeding Between Helping and Sharing-A Qualitative Study in Türkiye.
papers.journal: Breastfeeding medicine : the official journal of the Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Breastfeeding has traditionally been regarded as confined to the mother-infant dyad, and fathers' experiences of this process remain underexplored. This qualitative study explored, from their own perspectives, the experiences of fathers who reported supporting their partners during breastfeeding. DESIGN AND METHODS: A qualitative descriptive study was conducted with 16 fathers of breastfed children aged 0-24 months, purposively recruited from health care facilities in Zonguldak, Türkiye. Individual, face-to-face, semi-structured interviews were conducted between January and April 2026 and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis. Findings were interpreted in light of the distinction between helping with care work and sharing responsibility for it. RESULTS: Four main themes were identified: (1) The Process of Knowledge and Awareness; (2) From Active Partnership to Complementary Strength; (3) Emotional Experiences: Fluctuating Between Helplessness and Bonding; and (4) Sociocultural Context and the Health Care System: From Invisibility to Participatory Agency. Fathers reported providing domestic, practical, and emotional support, yet mostly described this support as "helping" and obtained breastfeeding information largely through their partners. Across themes, their involvement was mediated through their partners and peripheral to the mother-infant relationship; in health care settings, one father described himself as "the third person in the room." CONCLUSIONS: This selected group of supportive fathers saw themselves as active participants in breastfeeding; however, their accounts point to assistance within an existing division of labor rather than equally shared responsibility. Because the findings rest solely on fathers' self-reports, no inferences can be drawn about maternal well-being or breastfeeding outcomes. papers.title: Self-Assembly and Thermally Activated Bowl Inversion of Tetrabenzocorannulene Buckybowls on Ag(111).
papers.abstract: Bowl-shaped π-conjugated molecules possess a unique structural degree of freedom absent from planar nanographenes: bowl inversion. Understanding how this inversion couples to surface adsorption is essential for controlling the structure and function of curved molecular architectures. Here we show that the conformation of tetrabenzocorannulene (TBC) on Ag(111) is determined by the competition between intermolecular packing and molecule-substrate interactions. By tuning the annealing temperature and duration, we induce transitions between self-assembled phases dominated by concave-face-up and concave-face-down conformations. Scanning tunneling microscopy combined with density functional theory reveals that these phases are stabilized by different interaction regimes, with intermolecular interactions favoring concave-face-up structures and stronger substrate bonding stabilizing concave-face-down configurations. Our results establish molecular curvature as a thermodynamically tunable degree of freedom in surface-supported molecular assemblies, providing a general strategy for controlling the structure of curved π-conjugated nanocarbons.

papers.title: The Psychological and Relational Impact of Mayer-Rokitansky-Kuster-Hauser Syndrome: Perspectives of Patients, Mothers and Partners.
papers.journal: The Australian & New Zealand journal of obstetrics & gynaecology
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome (MRKHS) is a rare reproductive disorder with long-term psychosocial impacts. However, understanding of family and partner relationships that integrates the perspectives of patients, parents, and partners remains limited. AIMS: To evaluate the psychosocial impact of MRKHS with a focus on psychological and relational functioning, from patient, parent, and partner perspectives in an Australian cohort. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with MRKHS aged ≥ 18 years (n = 23), their parents (n = 8), and partners (n = 3) were recruited from a tertiary centre in Sydney, Australia. Three tailored questionnaires used validated self-report measures to assess physical and psychological health, family functioning, relationship satisfaction, fertility-related quality of life (QoL), sexual function, and personal identity. Comparison data were drawn from published validation studies. RESULTS: Patients with MRKHS reported comparable self-perceived health and relationship satisfaction to reference groups, but higher anxiety (p = 0.002), more significant dyspareunia (p = 0.006), and poorer perceived family functioning (p < 0.001). They reported better overall fertility-related QoL than couples undergoing fertility treatment (p = 0.03) but had lower scores on the relationship subscale (p = 0.002). MRKHS had a central impact shaping self-identity (p = 0.002). Mothers and partners reported positive wellbeing and family or relationship functioning, although the findings are preliminary due to the limited sample size. CONCLUSION: MRKHS affects multiple facets of patients' lives, particularly psychological well-being, pain-related sexual function, family dynamics, and personal identity. papers.title: Psychological resilience among informal care partners of individuals with mild cognitive impairment.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Care partners of individuals with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) encounter unique psychosocial and operational challenges. While dementia research traditionally focuses on advanced cognitive decline, the factors underlying positive psychological adaptation during the early MCI window remain poorly characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of psychological resilience among informal care partners of individuals with MCI and identify independent multivariable correlates of high adaptive capacity. METHODS: We conducted a multicenter, cross-sectional study across 19 specialized memory clinics in Spain in collaboration with the Spanish Confederation of Alzheimer's Disease and Other Dementias (CEAFA). Psychological resilience was quantified using the 14-Item Resilience Scale (RS-14). Secondary outcomes included health-related quality of life, caregiver strain, psychological distress, dyadic relationship quality, and perceived affiliate stigma. Multivariable logistic regression was employed to identify independent predictors of moderate-to-high resilience (RS-14 score >81). RESULTS: We analyzed 196 care partners (mean age: 63.5 [SD 13.1] years, 62.8% women). Overall, 63.3% (n = 124) demonstrated moderate-to-high resilience. In bivariate analyses, higher resilience correlated with superior quality of life, greater sense of competence, and enhanced relationship quality between care partners and care recipients. In multivariable logistic regression, only robust perceived social support (OR=2.37, 95% CI 1.78-3.14, p < 0.001) and lower affiliate stigma (OR=0.09, 95% CI 0.03-0.23, p < 0.001) remained independently associated with moderate-to-high resilience (model fit: Hosmer- Lemeshow x2  = 5.039, p = 0.753; Nagelkerke R2 = 0.319). papers.title: From Spark to Strain? Changes in Relationship Satisfaction as a Function of Narcissistic Admiration and Rivalry.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Narcissism is often proposed to drive attraction early in relationships but ultimately leads to poor long-term outcomes that are distressing to narcissistic individuals' partners. We examined changes in relationship satisfaction over a six-year period as a function of narcissistic admiration and narcissistic rivalry. METHOD: Data came from 5869 romantic dyads and a subsample of 533 early relationships within their first year. Participants were part of the German Family Panel (pairfam). Respondents completed the short form of the Narcissistic Admiration and Rivalry Questionnaire. For 6 years, both respondents and their partners completed a single-item relationship satisfaction measure. RESULTS: Both one's own and one's partner's narcissistic rivalry were associated with lower satisfaction in the full sample, but not the new relationships sample. Narcissistic admiration was not significantly associated with satisfaction. Contrary to predictions, neither partner's narcissism moderated relationship satisfaction changes in either sample. CONCLUSIONS: Despite its association with lower baseline satisfaction, narcissistic rivalry failed to moderate longitudinal changes in relationship satisfaction. These findings challenge the assumption of a linear cost to narcissism over time and highlight the need to investigate alternative time scales or heterogeneous relationship outcomes.
